fixed_requirements: Next-token prediction on the frozen task corpus with its fixed tokenizer (vocabulary 4096), context length 512, and batch 32
Causal prefix access only: the prediction at t depends only on tokens <= t of the same sequence
No state carried across sequences, batch rows, or evaluation calls
Equal training-FLOP budget per candidate, counted as executed, with the same data order and init seed for paired comparison
Evaluator, data splits, and engineering checks are fixed; the confirm split is sealed
editable_priors: Matched training FLOPs is the fair comparison (rather than matched parameters or wall-clock)
Early-checkpoint dev loss is informative about longer-run dev loss (Stage A tests this)
Results reported at 70M-8B transfer qualitatively to 5-30M models
Average next-token loss is the primary utility; mechanism-specific probes are diagnostics
permitted_constructions: Any torch modules, including custom recurrences over depth or sequence within one forward pass
Per-token adaptive computation, with an auxiliary loss returned as aux_loss
Parameter sharing, routing, gating, extra latent positions, or new state variables within a sequence
Recipe changes within the allowed train_config bounds

nodes.statement: At each layer l the model's state for a sequence is one hidden vector h_t^l in R^d per position t; the prediction at t reads only states at positions <= t.
sources: arXiv:1706.03762 Vaswani+ 2017, Attention Is All You Need

nodes.statement: Sequence mixing moves information between positions (attention, convolution, or recurrence); channel mixing transforms each position's vector on its own (feed-forward layers).
sources: arXiv:2403.17844 Poli+ 2024, Mechanistic Design and Scaling of Hybrid Architectures (MAD)

nodes.statement: Compute is FLOPs as executed: per-token cost is the FLOPs spent on one position in one forward pass; training cost is total executed training FLOPs, the fixed budget each candidate receives in this study.
sources: arXiv:2001.08361 Kaplan+ 2020, Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
cspace profile on this harness (measured, Nov 2026)

nodes.statement: Associative recall: predicting a token by retrieving the value bound to a key that appeared earlier in the context (multi-query associative recall, MQAR); induction heads are the attention mechanism for it.
sources: arXiv:2209.11895 Olsson+ 2022, In-context Learning and Induction Heads

nodes.statement: Every position receives the same computation: L blocks, each applied exactly once, in a fixed order.
sources: arXiv:1706.03762 Vaswani+ 2017, Attention Is All You Need

nodes.statement: Each block has its own parameters, so parameter count grows linearly with depth and no computation is reused across depth.
sources: arXiv:1706.03762 Vaswani+ 2017, Attention Is All You Need

nodes.statement: The unit of state and computation is the input token: no extra latent positions (memory or register tokens), and positions are never merged, split, or skipped.
sources: arXiv:1706.03762 Vaswani+ 2017, Attention Is All You Need

nodes.statement: Sequence memory is the uncompressed set of all past keys and values at every layer, read by causal softmax attention; memory grows linearly with context and is never summarized.
sources: arXiv:1706.03762 Vaswani+ 2017, Attention Is All You Need
nodes.notes: Justified mainly by recall: attention is the strongest known mechanism for associative recall.

nodes.statement: Information passes between blocks through one additive residual stream of width d: h^{l+1} = h^l + f_l(norm(h^l)). Block outputs are summed, never gated, weighted by depth, or routed between multiple streams.
sources: arXiv:1706.03762 Vaswani+ 2017, Attention Is All You Need

nodes.statement: Channel mixing is one dense SwiGLU feed-forward layer per block, applied identically to every token.
sources: arXiv:2002.05202 Shazeer 2020, GLU Variants Improve Transformer

nodes.statement: Position enters only through rotary embeddings applied to attention queries and keys; there is no absolute position embedding.
nodes.notes: RoPE is a construction on attention queries and keys, so it depends on the attention memory.

nodes.statement: Each sublayer input is normalized with RMSNorm (pre-norm); queries, keys, and block outputs are not normalized.
sources: arXiv:2002.04745 Xiong+ 2020, On Layer Normalization in the Transformer Architecture

nodes.statement: The input embedding and the output projection share one matrix.
sources: arXiv:1608.05859 Press & Wolf 2016, Using the Output Embedding
arXiv:1611.01462 Inan+ 2016, Tying Word Vectors and Word Classifiers

nodes.statement: Queries and keys are RMS-normalized per head before rotary embedding, bounding attention logits.
sources: arXiv:2309.14322 Wortsman+ 2023, Small-scale proxies for training instabilities

nodes.statement: Llama-style causal decoder (Transformer++ with QK-norm): the starting formulation, assembled from the commitments above.
nodes.scope: d_model 256, 6 layers, 4 heads: 5.9M parameters at vocabulary 4096
sources: arXiv:2403.17844 Poli+ 2024, Mechanistic Design and Scaling of Hybrid Architectures (MAD)
cspace profile on this harness (measured, Nov 2026)

nodes.statement: Under c.kv_memory, attention compute per token and inference memory grow linearly with the position in the context.
sources: arXiv:1706.03762 Vaswani+ 2017, Attention Is All You Need

nodes.statement: Under c.fixed_depth and c.dense_ffn, every token gets identical executed FLOPs regardless of how hard it is to predict.
Under c.fixed_depth, the serial computation available to a prediction within one forward pass is bounded by the L block applications; more serial steps require more depth, iteration, or extra tokens.
nodes.scope: conditional on a fixed, non-iterated stack
sources: arXiv:2301.13196 Giannou+ 2023, Looped Transformers as Programmable Computers
nodes.notes: Formal circuit-complexity bounds for fixed-depth transformers exist, but no citation for them was verified in this sweep.

nodes.statement: Causal attention with a kernel feature map in place of softmax is a recurrence with a fixed-size matrix state updated by outer products; it trains in parallel and generates recurrently.
sources: arXiv:2102.11174 Schlag+ 2021, Linear Transformers Are Secretly Fast Weight Programmers

nodes.statement: Linear attention is equivalent to a fast-weight programmer; purely additive outer-product updates have limited memory capacity, which motivates error-correcting (delta-rule) updates.
sources: arXiv:2102.11174 Schlag+ 2021, Linear Transformers Are Secretly Fast Weight Programmers

nodes.statement: Fixed-state gated-convolution models trail attention by up to 2.1 perplexity on the Pile; tokens that need associative recall (6.4% of tokens) account for about 82% of the gap; a 70M attention model beats a 1.4B gated-convolution model on recall.
nodes.scope: 17 models, 70M-1.4B, Pile; 2023-era gated convolutions (predates Mamba-2 and DeltaNet)

nodes.statement: Recall quality trades off against recurrent state size: fixed-state models (H3, Mamba, RWKV) struggle on recall-intensive tasks, and varying window size and feature dimension traces a recall-memory frontier.
sources: arXiv:2402.18668 Arora+ 2024, Simple linear attention LMs balance the recall-throughput tradeoff (BASED)

nodes.statement: A little attention recovers most of the recall gap: input-dependent sparse-attention hybrids close 97.4% of the Pile perplexity gap, and a 125M H3+attention hybrid beats a Transformer by 1.0 perplexity on OpenWebText.
Gated linear attention nearly matches Transformer++: WikiText perplexity 28.65 vs 28.39 at 340M (15B tokens) and 17.22 vs 16.85 at 1.3B (100B tokens).
sources: arXiv:2312.06635 Yang+ 2023, Gated Linear Attention Transformers

nodes.statement: Delta-rule updates beat additive linear attention on WikiText-103 at about 40M and 90M parameters; pure linear models still underperform Transformers on in-context retrieval at 1.3B; gated delta rules outperform Mamba2 and DeltaNet.
sources: arXiv:2102.11174 Schlag+ 2021, Linear Transformers Are Secretly Fast Weight Programmers
arXiv:2406.06484 Yang+ 2024, Parallelizing Linear Transformers with the Delta Rule

nodes.statement: Selective state-space models match same-size Transformers on language modeling at billion scale; Mamba-2 trains 2-8x faster than Mamba while remaining competitive.
sources: arXiv:2405.21060 Dao & Gu 2024, Transformers are SSMs (Mamba-2)
arXiv:2406.07887 Waleffe+ 2024, An Empirical Study of Mamba-based Language Models

nodes.statement: A k-layer block looped L times nearly matches a kL-layer model on synthetic reasoning and is competitive on downstream reasoning; looped transformers fit in-context learning tasks with under 10% of the parameters.
nodes.scope: synthetic tasks and LM reasoning; sizes not stated in abstracts
sources: arXiv:2502.17416 Saunshi+ 2025, Reasoning with Latent Thoughts
arXiv:2311.12424 Yang+ 2023, Looped Transformers are Better at Learning Learning Algorithms
nodes.notes: Motivated by t.depth_bound; the evidence stands on its own experiments.

nodes.statement: A shared recursive block with learned per-token recursion depth (Mixture-of-Recursions) lowers validation perplexity at equal training FLOPs with fewer parameters.

Learned adaptive computation (ACT) gives large gains on synthetic algorithmic tasks but small gains on character-level language modeling; adaptive per-layer looping mainly helps math reasoning, with gated memory recovering commonsense performance.
nodes.scope: ACT: char-level LM; adaptive loops: 2026 workshop preprint
sources: arXiv:2603.08391 (2026), Adaptive Loops and Memory in Transformers (workshop preprint)

nodes.statement: Routing a capacity-limited subset of tokens through each block (Mixture-of-Depths) matches baseline quality at equivalent training FLOPs and wall-clock, with faster steps at sampling.
Per-token early exit and self-speculative decoding cut inference compute (roughly 2-3x) while keeping quality.
nodes.scope: inference-time savings on Llama-family models; not rewarded by this study's training-FLOP budget
sources: arXiv:2207.07061 Schuster+ 2022, Confident Adaptive Language Modeling

nodes.statement: Learnable memory tokens improve translation and language modeling; memory tokens passed between segments make a recurrent model on par with Transformer-XL; a 3.2M single-block UT with ACT reaches non-trivial Sudoku-Extreme accuracy only with memory tokens.
nodes.scope: mixed; the Sudoku result is one task and one preprint
sources: arXiv:2604.21999 (2026), Universal Transformers Need Memory (single-author preprint)

nodes.statement: Depth-weighted averaging of earlier block outputs (DenseFormer) improves perplexity with a few thousand extra parameters; multiple residual streams with learned connections (hyper-connections) report significant gains over residual connections; constraining them to a manifold restores the identity mapping.
nodes.scope: author-reported; model sizes not stated in abstracts
sources: arXiv:2603.14833 (2026), Ablate and Rescue: residual-stream hyper-connections

nodes.statement: Immediate block-wise weight sharing improves accuracy at no parameter cost (+0.7% and +0.8% at 125M and 350M); cross-layer sharing cuts parameters substantially in BERT-scale encoders.
sources: arXiv:2104.06022 Takase & Kiyono 2021, Lessons on Parameter Sharing across Layers

nodes.statement: Evidence on depth versus width conflicts: over a wide range shape matters little relative to parameter count (Kaplan); at fixed parameters deeper models generalize more compositionally (41M-374M); deep-and-thin is chosen at 125M-350M.
sources: arXiv:2001.08361 Kaplan+ 2020, Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
arXiv:2310.19956 Petty+ 2023, Impact of Depth on Compositional Generalization

nodes.statement: Models under 10M parameters trained on TinyStories produce coherent English.
Fine-grained experts beat feed-forward-sized experts across compute budgets, and the dense-versus-MoE efficiency gap widens with scale.
nodes.scope: about 129M-3.7B on C4; no evidence at 5-30M
sources: arXiv:2402.07871 Krajewski+ 2024, Scaling Laws for Fine-Grained MoE

nodes.statement: GLU-family feed-forward layers (SwiGLU, GEGLU) improve over ReLU and GELU feed-forward layers.
sources: arXiv:2002.05202 Shazeer 2020, GLU Variants Improve Transformer

nodes.statement: Pre-norm removes the learning-rate warmup that post-norm needs; RMSNorm matches LayerNorm and is cheaper.
sources: arXiv:2002.04745 Xiong+ 2020, On Layer Normalization in the Transformer Architecture

nodes.statement: Large-scale instabilities (attention-logit growth, output-logit divergence) reproduce in small models at high learning rates, and QK-normalization and z-loss mitigate them.
sources: arXiv:2309.14322 Wortsman+ 2023, Small-scale proxies for training instabilities

nodes.statement: Causal LMs without positional encoding remain competitive and learn position implicitly; no positional encoding length-generalizes better than RoPE or ALiBi on downstream reasoning; ALiBi extrapolates beyond its training length.
sources: arXiv:2203.16634 Haviv+ 2022, Transformer LMs without Positional Encodings
arXiv:2305.19466 Kazemnejad+ 2023, Positional Encoding and Length Generalization

nodes.statement: At small scale embeddings are a large share of parameters (18% of the 5.9M baseline at vocabulary 4096), and tying is standard in small-model recipes.
sources: cspace profile on this harness (measured, Nov 2026)
arXiv:1608.05859 Press & Wolf 2016, Using the Output Embedding

nodes.statement: Average perplexity can hide recall deficits, and simple synthetic recall tests can miss language-model behavior; MAD's synthetic tasks are reported to predict compute-optimal perplexity.
sources: arXiv:2403.17844 Poli+ 2024, Mechanistic Design and Scaling of Hybrid Architectures (MAD)

nodes.statement: Universal Transformer: one shared block applied recurrently over depth with per-position dynamic halting.
PonderNet: probabilistic halting that learns the number of steps end to end.
Recurrent-depth LM: prelude, a core block iterated a variable number of times, and coda; test-time compute scales in latent space.
sources: arXiv:2502.17416 Saunshi+ 2025, Reasoning with Latent Thoughts
arXiv:2301.13196 Giannou+ 2023, Looped Transformers as Programmable Computers

nodes.statement: Mixture-of-Recursions: shared recursive block with per-token routing to different recursion depths.
Mixture-of-Depths: a router sends only top-k tokens through each block; others skip it on the residual stream.
Early exit: tokens stop at an intermediate layer once confident.
sources: arXiv:2207.07061 Schuster+ 2022, Confident Adaptive Language Modeling

nodes.statement: Linear or gated linear attention: a fixed-size matrix state replaces the KV history; log-linear variants grow the state logarithmically.
sources: arXiv:2312.06635 Yang+ 2023, Gated Linear Attention Transformers

nodes.statement: Delta-rule state updates (DeltaNet, Gated DeltaNet, RWKV-7): the state is corrected toward new key-value pairs instead of summed.
sources: arXiv:2406.06484 Yang+ 2024, Parallelizing Linear Transformers with the Delta Rule

nodes.statement: State-space sequence mixing (S4, Mamba, Mamba-2): input-dependent linear recurrence with a fixed-size state.
sources: arXiv:2405.21060 Dao & Gu 2024, Transformers are SSMs (Mamba-2)

nodes.statement: Retention and RWKV-style recurrences with parallel training and recurrent inference.
Local (sliding-window) attention combined with a recurrent or linear-attention layer (Griffin, Samba, BASED, Jamba).
sources: arXiv:2402.18668 Arora+ 2024, Simple linear attention LMs balance the recall-throughput tradeoff (BASED)

nodes.statement: Memory or register tokens: extra latent positions that read and write global state.
sources: arXiv:2309.16588 Darcet+ 2023, Vision Transformers Need Registers

nodes.statement: Hyper-connections: several residual streams with learned depth and width connections.
Learned access to earlier layers: depth-weighted averaging (DenseFormer) or gated highway paths.
Cross-layer or block-wise weight sharing.
sources: arXiv:2104.06022 Takase & Kiyono 2021, Lessons on Parameter Sharing across Layers

nodes.statement: Sparse mixture-of-experts feed-forward layers with learned routing.
ALiBi distance biases or no positional encoding (NoPE).
sources: arXiv:2203.16634 Haviv+ 2022, Transformer LMs without Positional Encodings

nodes.statement: Output z-loss: an auxiliary penalty on the log-partition of the output logits for logit stability.
sources: arXiv:2309.14322 Wortsman+ 2023, Small-scale proxies for training instabilities
